entry.summary:
<h2>Using CWAC to test websites</h2>
<p>The GCDO is using the Centralised Web Accessibility Checker (CWAC — pronounced ‘quack’) to test for accessibility errors on the publicly facing government websites of:</p>
<ul>
<li>agencies mandated to meet the NZ Government Web Standards — public service departments, NZ Defence Force, NZ Police and the Parliamentary Counsel Office</li>
<li>other agencies who have agreed to participate.</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://www.digital.govt.nz/standards-and-guidance/nz-government-web-standards/centralised-web-accessibility-checker-cwac">Centralised Web Accessibility Checker (CWAC)</a></p>
<p>In addition to raising the profile of accessibility within government agencies, the monitoring programme will:</p>
<ul>
<li>help create a system-level overview of automatically detectable accessibility errors across government websites</li>
<li>provide actionable insights for agencies on how to improve the accessibility of their websites.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Quarterly scans</h2>
<p>At the end of every quarter, starting <time datetime="2025-6-30">30 June 2025</time>, CWAC will scan up to 100 pages from each participating agency’s publicly facing websites.</p>
<p>CWAC crawls each website, much like Google, randomly selecting the pages to test. Every time a website is scanned, CWAC is likely to test a number of different pages from that site.</p>
<p>As it scans, CWAC stores the accessibility data for each web page in CSV files.</p>
<h2>Publishing the results and agency leaderboards</h2>
<h3>Results on Data.govt.nz</h3>
<p>Following each quarterly scan, the raw results are published on Data.govt.nz.</p>
<p><a href="https://catalogue.data.govt.nz/dataset/centralised-web-accessibility-checker-cwac-monitoring-programme#dataset-resources">CWAC results — Data.govt.nz</a></p>
<div class="callout-note callout--no-title" role="note">
<p>The data that CWAC produces is not private. CWAC only reads publicly available web pages. The results it creates can be reproduced by anyone who:</p>
<ul>
<li>uses the same free and open-source components that CWAC does</li>
<li>downloads and uses CWAC from GitHub</li>
<li>uses free and readily available browser plugins that do the same thing.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p>Openly publishing the CWAC results to Data.govt.nz:</p>
<ul>
<li>contributes to the government’s obligations under the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) to monitor and report on the implementation of minimum accessibility standards — this helps ensure New Zealand remains accountable and continues to improve the lives of disabled people</li>
<li>demonstrates a commitment to open data and transparent government</li>
<li>saves time answering Official Information Act requests on CWAC data.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Leaderboards on Digital.govt.nz</h3>
<p>Following the <time datetime="2025-9">September 2025 quarterly scan, agency and website CWAC scores will be published on Digital.govt.nz.</time></p>
<p>An agency leaderboard will list each participating agency alongside its CWAC score.</p>
<h2>Contact the team</h2>
<p>If you have any questions related to CWAC or the Web Accessibility Standard, email <a href="mailto:web.standards@gdda.govt.nz?subject=CWAC%20monitoring%20programme">web.standards@gdda.govt.nz</a>.</p>
